A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SparseVLM work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video benchmark experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including retained experiments and additional Qwen2-VL evaluations and efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: The core text-rater selection, rank-based pruning and token-recycling procedures remain unchanged. v3 Appendix A.2 newly specifies two FlashAttention passes, a special V matrix and output masking, but v1 already states that FlashAttention is used. The PDFs do not establish whether this is a new inference adaptation or documentation of the existing implementation.

E1.justification: The main benchmark comparison replaces VQAv2 and ConBench with SEED-Bench and MMVet, adding different data and integrated-capability evaluation while removing the explicit consistency benchmark. VQAv2 remains described in v3's appendix, but its former quantitative comparison is absent. The four video benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds the training-free PDrop/PyramidDrop comparator to every token-budget group in Table 1, alongside the retained ToMe and FastV methods. Figures 9–10 additionally compare SparseVLM against random pruning, substantially extending the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The stated video token budget changes from 135 to 198, and the text-rater ablation changes from 142 to 64 retained tokens. v3 also introduces Qwen2-VL evaluations at 600, 500 and 400 tokens. The changed video setting does not establish that its unchanged accuracy entries were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds latency/FLOPs–accuracy tradeoff analyses for LLaVA and MGM and latency/token-budget analyses for Video-LLaVA in Figures 9–11, including random-pruning and full-query controls. It also revises the rater-selection ablation and replaces TextVQA with GQA in the recycling ablation while retaining POPE.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The additional random-pruning comparisons do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous entries change: at 64 tokens, Table 1 reports SparseVLM POPE accuracy as 75.1 in v1 and 77.5 in v3, while FastV changes from 48.0 to 38.2. The reported efficiency baseline changes from 419.9 ms/9.6 TFLOPs to 57.82 ms/4.62 TFLOPs. v3 adds Qwen2-VL and tradeoff results; the video table retains accuracy values but removes per-dataset GPT scores. Changed coverage and incompletely reconciled settings prevent treating the revisions as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A.2 adds a mathematical construction for the special V matrix, blockwise attention accumulation and top-k extraction used in its FlashAttention description. The existing rank-based pruning rule and computational-cost derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central training-free, text-guided sparsification contribution is retained. The abstract's quantitative claim changes from 61–67% FLOPs reduction with 93% retained accuracy to 54% FLOPs reduction, 37% lower latency and 97% retained accuracy; the introduction also revises the claimed margins over FastV.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the Qwen2-VL results as evidence of compatibility with variable image resolutions. It also adds discussion of PDrop's lower FLOPs but worse measured latency and average accuracy, emphasizing deployment costs beyond FLOPs. The existing pruning and recycling mechanism explanations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 supplies substantial previously missing documentation of FlashAttention integration, including the two passes, special V matrix, token selection and masking. v3 also adds a Qwen inference/code reference. The stated hardware, software versions and SparseVLM code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the token-merging related-work subsection, including the LLaVolta discussion and explicit TCFormer inspiration/distinction. It adds citations and discussion for PyramidDrop, SEED-Bench and MMVet. The principal positioning around training-free, text-guided compression remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work and conclusion undergo broad rewriting and compression. Section titles and terminology are revised, the appendices are reorganized, and an Impact Statement is added. These changes extend beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Table 1 expands to include FLOPs and latency, the standalone efficiency table is removed, a Qwen2-VL table and Figures 9–11 are added, and the video table loses its score columns. Figure 6 contracts from seven examples to three; the appendix Figure 8 gallery is retained.

improvement.justification: The added PDrop comparisons, Qwen2-VL evaluation, cost–accuracy curves and FlashAttention documentation strengthen the paper's evidence and reproducibility. However, v3 Table 4 revises the recycling results while Section 5.2 retains v1's conflicting TextVQA and POPE gains. Its conclusion also reports 37% latency reduction at 77.8% compression, whereas Table 1's corresponding 128-token row implies about 42.4%. These reporting inconsistencies weaken confidence in the revised evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
